title: Physics of Information — Entropy, Energy, and Computation
content_html:
Physics of Information

Entropy, Energy, and Computation

The physics of information treats information as a physical quantity embodied in states and correlations. Shannon’s uncertainty measure links to statistical entropy through probabilities; Landauer’s principle shows that erasing information dissipates at least k_B T × ⁡ \ln 2 of heat per bit; and quantum theory constrains copying (no‑cloning) and accessible information (Holevo bound). These ideas set ultimate limits on memory, computation, and communication—from chips to black holes.

Arrows denote conceptual bridges: Jaynes (info ↔ entropy), Holevo/No‑cloning (quantum limits), Landauer (energy cost of erasure).
